target_customer: Non-developers and small teams who want full-stack apps from natural language with code ownership
problem: No-code tools are limited and costly; custom development is slow and expensive for non-engineers.
business_model: Subscription AI app builder, details not verified

founders.name: Uladzislau Radkevich
prior_employers: Revolut (led technical side of crypto development per YC bio)
founders.background_notes: Computer security background; hackathon wins per YC bio.

founders.name: Andrew Kim
previous_startups: Software outsourcing agency he ran (outcome not stated)

technical_complexity.rationale: Prompt to full-stack app generation on third party LLMs needs code generation, scaffolding and hosting integration, standard engineering with hard quality problems.

defensibility.rationale: Many well funded app builders (v0, Bolt, Lovable) offer the same wedge and models are shared.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Vercel v0, Bolt.new, Lovable and Replit became established alternatives per 2026 comparison pages; co.dev is still listed as active.

market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand at the batch was found; the YC launch post for the product is dated November 2024.

branding.domain_note: Uses the short co.dev domain; acquisition history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: The .dev domain hack is short, but the name is generic and collides with Codev and CoDev staffing; no brand coverage.

outcome_analysis: co.dev is a two person team still listed active in 2026 with a Prisma Postgres integration case study. Funding beyond YC is unverified. The AI app builder category was crowded by v0, Bolt and Lovable, so differentiation is the key risk, though no failure has been reported.
notes: Startup-Seeker estimates about $500K raised; single aggregator, unverified. co.dev site fetch returned only a title. A Prisma post quotes a co-founder named Andrew without a surname; the link to Andrew Kim relies on the YC bio. No dated 2023 competitors found; v0 and others are cited only from 2025 and 2026 lists.
